feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. Evidence from earlier races: iteration 1 (best, 114.4) had oval progress 0.47, oval steering_oscillation 0.28 and max_error 0.061 to 0.066 m. Iteration 4 (lighter, faster drivetrain) raised oscillation to 0.33 without a progress gain, so extra responsiveness is not helping. Iterations 5 and 6 showed the sensor lead is near its optimum at 0.03 m: 0.02 m dropped s-bend progress to 0.11, and 0.04 m gave 109.9 with s-bend progress 0.246 against 0.256 at 0.03 m. The sensor array and footprint should stay at the iteration-1 layout. For this candidate the Integrator kept the iteration-1 controller unchanged (kp 2.5, kd 0.30, base_speed 1.5, last_direction), so the only variable is wheel_track. Integration point: a wider track lowers yaw rate per wheel differential by about 9 percent, so the controller sees a softer turn response with the same gains. Change the next design by what the race shows. If steering_oscillation falls below about 0.28 while oval progress holds at or above 0.47 and max_error is at or below 0.06 m, keep the wider track and try mass 0.7 kg for bend damping. If oscillation falls but oval progress drops below about 0.44, the track has gone too far, so return to 0.10 m or try 0.105 m. If oscillation is unchanged or rises, the wheel track is not the limit, and mass or the drivetrain must change instead.
requested_changes: If steering_oscillation falls below 0.28 on the oval while progress holds at or above 0.47 but max_error stays at or above 0.06 m, set mass to 0.7 kg (from 0.6). Iteration 1 showed max_error of 0.064 to 0.066 m with small rms_error, so the excursion looks like bend overshoot that extra yaw inertia should damp.

If oval progress falls below 0.44 with lower oscillation, set wheel_track to 0.105 m (between 0.10 and 0.11). Iteration 1 at 0.10 m gave oval progress 0.47, so a smaller step should keep most of that progress while reducing oscillation.
Keep sensor y at 0.03 m and the five-sensor 12 mm layout. Iteration 5 (0.02 m lead) gave 91.8 and iteration 6 (0.04 m lead) gave 109.9, both below iteration 1 (114.4).
